Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

end verb

bring to an end

also put an end to, bring to an end, finish, wind up

classical

Cic. Sest. 136: dīcendī fīnem facere (Lewis & Short)
Verg. A. 3.718: factōque hīc fīne quiēvit

fīnem facere

phrase, with the genitive of a gerund or the dative

put an end to, stop

dīcendī fīnem faciam, I’ll stop talking; with the dative, fīnem injūriīs factūrum (Caes. BG 1.33.1).

Other words

  • fīniō, fīnīre, fīnīvī, fīnītum — end, finish, put an end to

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · classical · Mart. 13.36.2: fīnit olīva dapēs; Caes. BC 3.51.3: bellum fīnīre (Lewis & Short); Traupman 309

    Its first sense is to mark the limits of something (Lewis & Short).

  • fīnem impōnere (+ dat.) — put an end to

    also used · classical · Quint. 9.4.146: fīnem impōnere volūminī; Liv. 5.4.10 (Lewis & Short s.v. impōnō); Traupman 97

Examples

  • sīc pater Aenēās intentīs omnibus ūnus fāta renarrābat dīvum cursūsque docēbat. conticuit tandem factōque hīc fīne quiēvit

    So father Aeneas alone, with all of them listening, told again of the fates the gods had sent and taught them his wanderings. At last he fell silent, made an end here, and rested.Verg. A. 3.716–718

  • haec quae Pīcēnīs venit subducta trapētīs inchoat atque eadem fīnit olīva dapēs

    this olive, fresh from the Picene presses, begins the meal, and the same olive ends itMart. 13.36.1–2

  • permittētis tamen fīnīrī lūsum

    but you’ll let me finish my gamePetr. 33.1

  • bellī fīnem facere

    to put an end to a warTraupman 309

See also end, end, stop, stop it!, begin.
